newsitem.title: USA: Search Capital enters $9 mln settlement.
newsitem.headline: Search Capital enters $9 mln settlement.

text.p: Search Capital Group Inc said Friday it had entered a settlement under which it will pay $4 million cash and a $5 million note in exchange for Phoenix/Inwood's stake in Search.
Phoenix/Inwood is a company controlled by a Search director, Craig Hall.
James Leary, Search's vice chairman of finance, said Phoenix/Inwood holds about a 12 percent stake in Search on a fully diluted basis.
The settlement resolves litigation between Search and Hall, Phoenix/Inwood and Larry Levey, Search said.
Levey is also a Search director.

Search, a consumer finance company in the non-prime auto loan market, issued a public apology to Hall and Levey about "unfavorable publicity or misinformation that may have occurred as a result of this litigation."
Details of the litigation were not available, and Leary declined to discuss the matter.

Search does not have any immediate plans for the repurchased Search shares, except to put them in its treasury, Leary said. The shares could be used for an acquisition, a purchase of assets or a type of stock dividend, he said.
On a fully diluted basis, the company has 75 million shares outstanding, Leary said.
Search later said Hall and Levey filed suit in October seeking access to the company's books and records.
Search said it had filed suit against the two directors and Phoenix/Inwood, alleging fraud and breach of fiduciary duty.
Search said it had furnished Hall and Levey with most of the records they were seeking.
